# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)

# Intake Brief: Serial Seller: achievement manifest entry + Steamworks API name

## Problem Statement

The new **Serial Seller** challenge (`ch-serial-seller`) must map to a persistent Steam achievement like the existing 12 challenges. The challenge-side mapping is added in the parent item (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J); this item covers the cross-repo pieces required before the parent can be reviewed.

## Users

- **Producers**: Need the Steam achievement registered on the Steamworks partner backend.
- **Developers**: Need the manifest entry to exist before the drift guard test will pass.
- **Players**: Need the Serial Seller achievement to appear in-game alongside the existing 12 achievements.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` contains a `serial-seller` entry with `steamApiName: TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` and `hidden: false`.
2. The Steamworks partner backend declares the matching `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` achievement API name.
3. The `core` submodule pointer in the main-street repo is bumped to the commit containing the manifest change.
4. The manifest drift guard (`tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts`) passes with the parent's mapping in place.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The manifest lives in the `core` git submodule (a separate repository: `TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine`), requiring two repo operations.
- The `steamApiName` values must match exactly what is configured on the Steamworks partner backend, or Steam will silently drop the unlock.
- The achievement must not be hidden (`hidden: false`), consistent with the existing 12 challenges.
- The Steamworks backend configuration is a producer/external action that must be completed independently of code changes.

## Existing State

- 12 existing achievements in `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`, all with the pattern `TCE_MAIN_STREET_<UPPER_SNAKE_CASE>`.
- The manifest is validated by `validateAchievementManifest()` and the drift guard test.
- Precedent: MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC (bumping core submodule pointer).

## Desired Change

- Add one entry to the manifest for the Serial Seller achievement.
- Commit to the core repo and bump the submodule pointer in main-street.
- Coordinate with the producer to register the achievement on Steamworks.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` — Add `serial-seller` entry
- `core/` (git submodule) — Commit the manifest change
- `.gitmodules` / submodule index — Bump the submodule pointer

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J**: Sell 3 businesses challenge (parent, blocked by this item)
- **MS-0MUNO0M2I004TK04**: Wire Main Street challenges to Steam achievements (parent epic)
- **MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC**: Precedent for bumping core submodule pointer

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Steamworks backend delay**: If the producer has not yet registered the achievement on Steamworks, the achievement will not unlock for players even after code changes land. This is tracked as a separate action.
- **Scope creep**: Additional achievement metadata (e.g., icons, descriptions) may be desired later; record as a follow-up, not in scope for this item.
- **Submodule conflict**: Unlikely but possible if the core repo has concurrent changes; resolve by rebasing on latest core before bumping.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- This item was already sufficiently defined; no interview questions were asked. The description, scope, and acceptance criteria were clear and actionable.

## Dependency & audit resolution (2026-10-01)

Producer confirmed the Steamworks backend registration (AC2) is not yet done and requires a dependency chain. Two dependency items were created in the core project (CG store — the correct home for Steamworks backend work; worklog does not support cross-store dependency edges, so they are recorded here as cross-project references):

- **CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ** — Create the Steamworks project for Tableau Card Engine
- **CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1** — Register Main Street achievements on the Steamworks backend *(depends on CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ)*

**AC2 therefore remains unmet until CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1 completes.** This item carries the `do-not-delegate` tag while externally blocked so the downtime worker does not re-dispatch it.

**Merge state:** the item's work is integrated into `dev`/`origin/dev` as commit `dd11ea4` (core → `d2d1f322`). The stale feature branch (which referenced the superseded core commit `4a287d4`) was reset to `dd11ea4`.

**AC4 call:** the drift guard requires the parent challenge-side mapping from **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J** (which depends on this item, so no cycle is possible). AC4 is verified at parent integration time; the mapping is present uncommitted in the working tree today and will pass permanently once the parent lands.

# Intake Brief: Static docs site for local browsing (VitePress)

**Priority: Low** | **Type: Chore** | **Assignee: Map**

> Discovered from MS-0MUNB54KU005084C as the deferred option (B). Producer
> answers 2026-10-17: still wanted (Q1=A); **navigation-first** use case
> (Q2=A); **local dev tool only**, no CI publishing (Q3=B).

## Headline

Add a VitePress static docs site over the existing `docs/game/` and
`docs/dev/` trees so developers and content authors can browse the docs with
sidebar navigation and rendered Mermaid locally (`npm run docs`); no CI
publishing is required.

## Problem statement

The repo ships docs as a flat, two-tree Markdown forest (`docs/game/`,
`docs/dev/`). Without a site, readers must navigate raw files and there is no
sidebar nav, no search, and no unified landing page. Mermaid fences in docs
(`core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `the-build-gdd.md`) render only with a
Mermaid-aware viewer. A static docs site fixes browsing and renders Mermaid at
build time.

## Users

- **Developers** — need to browse game + dev docs with nav/search while
  working on the codebase.
  - *"As a developer, I want a docs site with sidebar navigation, so I can
    find the right doc faster without guessing file paths."*
- **Game designers / content authors** — need the gameplay reference plus the
  storyline graphs readable in place.
  - *"As a content designer, I want Mermaid diagrams rendered in the docs
    page, so the storyline shape is visible without a Mermaid tool."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Docs site generator** — `vitepress` (MIT) is added as a devDependency
   and a `npm run docs` script serves the docs site locally
   (`vitepress dev docs`); the site root is `docs/` and covers both the
   `docs/game/` and `docs/dev/` trees with sidebar navigation. The
   `docs/.vitepress/` build output is git-ignored and the toolchain stays a
   devDependency only (it never enters the game bundle).
   *Metric: `npm run docs` starts a local server; `npm run docs:build`
   (`vitepress build docs`) exits 0 and emits a static site; `git status`
   stays clean after a build.*
2. **Navigation** — a sidebar (`.vitepress/config.ts`) lists the `docs/game/`
   and `docs/dev/` documents with clear audiences; every top-level `.md` in
   both trees is reachable from the nav (no orphaned docs).
   *Metric: a test asserts every `.md` under `docs/game/` + `docs/dev/` is
   covered by the sidebar config.*
3. **Mermaid rendering** — mermaid code fences in docs render to visible
   diagrams in the built site; the existing committed storyline SVGs
   (`docs/game/assets/storyline-graph-*.svg`) remain usable and are linked or
   embedded as today.
   *Metric: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` and `the-build-gdd.md`
   render with visible diagrams in the built site.*
4. **No link breakage / no migration** — existing files stay in place under
   `docs/game/` and `docs/dev/`; existing relative links between docs keep
   working; the `docs-path-drift` guard test stays green (no
   `docs/main-street/` or `example-games/main-street/` strings in the new
   VitePress config).
   *Metric: full suite passes including `docs-path-drift.test.ts`.*
5. **Testing/validation** — a pure config-scan unit test validates the docs
   build config (nav coverage + no forbidden paths) with no
   Playwright/browser requirement, and the full project test suite passes
   with the new changes.
   *Metric: the nav-coverage test runs in the `unit` project and asserts every
   top-level `.md` under both trees is listed in the sidebar; `npm test` exits
   0.*
6. **All related documentation is updated** — `docs/README.md` (and/or a new
   `docs/index.md`) documents the docs site plus the `npm run docs` /
   `npm run docs:build` commands, and the README reflects the new scripts.
   *Metric: `docs/README.md` or `docs/index.md` mentions `npm run docs`, and
   the project README documents the docs scripts.*
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.
8. **Local-only, no CI** — no GitHub Pages or docs CI workflow/job is added;
   the `docs` scripts are for local use and the existing game Pages deploy
   workflow is unchanged.
   *Metric: no new or modified workflow file references the docs build; the
   existing deploy workflow is untouched.*
9. **Permissive licence** — `vitepress` and every new plugin/dependency are
   permissively licensed (MIT/Apache-2.0/CC0).
   *Metric: each new dependency's licence is checked and recorded in the
   implementation notes.*

## Constraints

- **Local-only, no CI** — no GitHub Pages workflow, no docs CI job
   (Q3=B). `docs` scripts are for local use; the existing game Pages deploy
   workflow is untouched.
- **Permissive licence** — `vitepress` (MIT) and any new plugin must be
   permissively licensed (MIT/Apache-2.0/CC0).
- **devDependency only** — the docs toolchain must not enter the game bundle.
- **No reorganisation** — files stay under `docs/game/` / `docs/dev/`; the
   two-tree structure and `docs/README.md` index remain.
- **Drift guard** — new VitePress files under `docs/` must not contain
   `example-games/main-street/` or `docs/main-street/` (scanned by
   `docs-path-drift.test.ts`).
- **Determinism/coverage** — the nav-coverage test must be stable and fast
   (no Playwright/browser requirement for the unit suite).

## Existing state (repo research)

- No docs-site generator present: devDeps include `vite`, `vitest`,
   `playwright`, `mermaid`, `sharp`, `tsx`, `vite-node`, but **no
   `vitepress`/`docusaurus`/`mkdocs`** anywhere in the repo or `core/`.
- `docs/` is plain Markdown: `docs/README.md` index, `docs/game/` (11 files +
   `storylines/` (5) + `assets/` with 5 storyline SVGs), `docs/dev/` (21 files +
   `assets/` (9) + `analysis/`).
- Mermaid fences exist in `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (:162),
   `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (:207, :617); the storyline graph
   ships as committed SVGs under `docs/game/assets/`.
- `docs-path-drift.test.ts` scans every text file under `docs/` for
   forbidden legacy paths; a `.vitepress/config.ts` (or `.mjs`) is a `.ts`
   text file and will be scanned — it must avoid those strings.
- Node v22.22.1 (VitePress requires Node ≥18 — satisfied).
- `.gitignore` has `dist/` and `dist-electron/`; VitePress build output
   (`docs/.vitepress/dist`) must be ignored (add `.vitepress` or
   `docs/.vitepress/dist`).

## Desired change

1. Add `vitepress` (devDependency) and a `docs` npm script.
2. Add `docs/.vitepress/config.ts` with sidebar nav for both trees
   (or `.mjs` if TS config is awkward with the repo's toolchain — prefer
   `.ts` since Vite toolchain is already TS).
3. Theme/plugin for Mermaid rendering (e.g. via the `vitepress-plugin-mermaid`
   or a mermaid pre-render step) so mermaid code fences become visible
   diagrams in the built site.
4. Add a nav-coverage test (`tests/main-street/`) asserting every top-level
   `.md` in both trees appears in the sidebar config, plus the drift-guard
   string check on the new config files.
5. Update `docs/README.md` (or add `docs/index.md`) to note the docs site and
   the `npm run docs` command.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `package.json` — add `vitepress` devDependency + `docs` / `docs:build` npm
  scripts.
- `docs/.vitepress/config.ts` — **new** VitePress config (title, sidebar,
  mermaid plugin).
- `docs/.vitepress/theme/…` and/or mermaid plugin wiring — **new**.
- `tests/main-street/docs-site-nav.test.ts` — **new** nav-coverage + drift-
  string test.
- `tests/main-street/docs-path-drift.test.ts` — existing drift guard; must
  stay green for the new `.vitepress` files.
- `.gitignore` — ignore `docs/.vitepress/` build output.
- `docs/README.md` and/or new `docs/index.md` — site introduction + `npm run
  docs` command.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUNB54KU005084C** — Render the storyline graph (Mermaid→SVG) — completed (v0.1.19); this item is its deferred option (B).
- **MS-0MUYLLYX80090370** — Link & document the rendered storyline graph — completed; embedded the SVG in the canonical doc and documented regeneration.
- **MS-0MUZK0OWJ000PQ2D** — Restructure documentation (two-tree split) — established `docs/game/` + `docs/dev/`.
- **MS-0MUNC8AOL0092BE5** — Fix stale `example-games/main-street` paths — owner of the `docs-path-drift` guard.
- **MS-0MUSY1M1F003IS47** — Editor host & read-only graph viewer (blocked) — may eventually consume the docs-rendered graphs.

## Assumptions

- The docs site is **local-only** (Q3=B): no CI build or Pages publishing is
  added; if publishing is wanted later it is a follow-up item.
- Navigation is the primary need (Q2=A); Mermaid fences are rendered in the
  built site (client-side rendering acceptable — see risk) and do not replace
  the committed `.mmd`/SVG pipeline.
- `nodemon`/live-reload behaviour from VitePress dev server is fine; no
  custom theme is needed beyond Mermaid support.

## Risks

- **Toolchain adoption (LOW–MED).** VitePress is Vite-native (repo already
  uses Vite), but its config adds a new docs toolchain. *Mitigation:*
  devDependency only; config kept small; no bundler changes.
- **Mermaid rendering approach (MED).** `vitepress-plugin-mermaid` renders
  client-side in the browser by default, not at build time; the item title
  says "at build time". *Mitigation:* either pre-render server-side (run the
  existing `mermaid` + Playwright render step during `docs:build`) or accept
  client-side rendering for the local dev use case (Q3=B); record the choice
  in the item at implementation.
- **Drift-guard interference (LOW).** New `.vitepress` files are scanned by
  `docs-path-drift.test.ts`. *Mitigation:* keep the forbidden strings out of
  new config; nav test covers coverage.
- **Scope creep risk.** Full-text search, versioning/multi-version docs,
  CI publishing, i18n, custom theming → out of scope; record as separate
  work items if requested.
- **Test determinism (LOW).** Nav test must not require a browser; keep it a
  pure config-scan unit test.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Still wanted?** Now that the minimal render step is shipped, is the
  larger static docs site still desired?
  - Options: (A) Still want it; (B) No longer needed.
  - **Recommended: (B).** Original problem solved by MS-0MUNB54KU005084C.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): (A)** — still build the static docs
    site. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Primary use case?**
  - Options: (A) Better navigation/structure; (B) Mermaid-at-render for all
    docs; (C) Both.
  - **Recommended: (A).**
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): (A)** — navigation-first; Mermaid
    rendering at build time remains in the title/scope but is not the sole
    driver. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Target audience / delivery?**
  - Options: (A) Internal/CI only (Pages); (B) Local dev tool (`npm run
    docs`); (C) Both.
  - **Recommended: (A).**
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): (B)** — local dev tool only; **no CI
    publishing**. Source: interactive reply.

> All three answers recorded in comment MS-C0MVBVDIK0006YSM7.

## Open Questions (from plan review)

- **OPEN QUESTION — build-time vs client-side Mermaid rendering.** The title
  says "render Mermaid docs at build time", but the Risks section permits
  client-side rendering for the local-only use case (Q3=B). Directed to the
  producer. Why it matters: a build-time pre-render needs a
  Playwright/Chromium step in `docs:build` (slower, more moving parts), while
  a client-side plugin keeps the build simple but ships Mermaid JS to the
  browser. Proposed default (does not block planning): client-side
  `vitepress-plugin-mermaid`, with the choice recorded in the item at
  implementation.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-19 — `/skill:plan` run: effort/risk pre-check returned **skip**
  (Extra Small, Low risk), so no decomposition was performed. Six-stage
  review applied conservatively: AC alignment (AC1 now covers the gitignore
  and devDependency-only constraints; AC8 added for local-only/no-CI; AC9 for
  permissive licence; AC5/AC6 tightened to measurable criteria), completeness
  (added the existing `docs-path-drift.test.ts` guard to Key Files),
  testability (nav test pinned to the `unit` project, no browser), polish
  (fixed the `vitepress build docs` typo). Open Question raised on build-time
  vs client-side Mermaid rendering.

# Migrate Main Street Renderer from Canvas to WebGL

**Related parent:** `MS-0MUWNTQ5L0075Y38` — Create a card shader (completed, Canvas-compatible effect delivered)

## Problem statement

The game currently boots with `type: Phaser.CANVAS`, which prevents the use of Phaser 4's Filter system and custom GPU shaders. A true GPU card shader (the goal of the parent work item) requires WebGL rendering. The renderer must be migrated to WebGL so that GPU-based effects become available in production.

## Users

- **Game players** — experience GPU-accelerated card shaders with correct visual quality.
- **Developers** — can use Phaser 4's Filter/postFX pipeline for rendering effects.
- **CI/automation** — browser tests continue to run efficiently in headless environments.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **WebGL boot:** The game boots under `Phaser.AUTO` (WebGL with Canvas fallback) in `main.ts` and `game-repo-scaffold.ts`, with no visual regression to existing rendering.
2. **GeometryMask migration:** All `Phaser.Display.Masks.GeometryMask` usages across Main Street and core UI are migrated to Phaser 4's `Mask` filter (or equivalent `createMask`/`addMaskShape` API). Verified across: `HelpPanel.ts`, `Overlay.ts`, `SettingsPanel.ts`, `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`, `MainStreetRendererHud.ts`, `MainStreetScene.ts`, `GymCardIndexScene.ts`, and `GymOverlayUiScene.ts`.
3. **WebGL browser test:** At least one browser test project exercises WebGL rendering (e.g., a Playwright-based Chromium + SwiftShader project that forces `Phaser.WEBGL` and validates rendering correctness).
4. **Test suite passes:** Full project test suite passes with WebGL rendering.
5. **Documentation updated:** All relevant documentation reflects the WebGL migration, including comments about the `type` field and mask API changes.

## Constraints

- **CI performance:** `TestGamePool` and browser tests intentionally use Canvas for speed (~10x faster under SwiftShader). This migration must not force tests to WebGL — test factories should continue to pass `type: Phaser.CANVAS` where appropriate.
- **GeometryMask is Canvas-only in Phaser 4 RC7:** `node_modules/phaser/src/display/mask/GeometryMask.js:27` explicitly states this. Must use the Phaser 4 `Mask` class (`scene.make.mask()` or `sprite.setMask(mask)`) as the replacement.
- **WebGL blend modes:** WebGL supports only NORMAL/ADD/MULTIPLY/SCREEN blend modes. Main Street does not use exotic blend modes, so no issue expected.
- **SVG textures:** `core/src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts` uses `textures.addCanvas` for SVG-derived card art. These must survive GPU re-upload in WebGL.
- **Context loss:** WebGL context loss/restoration is a new failure mode that must be considered.
- **Rendering determinism:** Visual output is not byte-identical across Canvas/WebGL/GPUs; visual regression checks may need adjustment.
- **Phaser version:** 4.0.0-rc.7 — ships only WebGL (no WebGPU). This is the intermediate step towards a future WebGL2/WebGPU backend.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `core/main.ts` — Change `type: Phaser.CANVAS` to `Phaser.AUTO`
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — Change `type: Phaser.CANVAS` to `Phaser.AUTO`
- `core/src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` — Replace `GeometryMask` with `Mask` filter
- `core/src/ui/Overlay.ts` — Replace `createGeometryMask()` with `createMask()`
- `core/src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — Replace `GeometryMask` with `Mask` filter
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — Replace `GeometryMask` with `Mask` filter (log mask + street map mask)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — Update any GeometryMask references
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — Update type declaration for `logContentMask`
- `src/gym/GymCardIndexScene.ts` — Replace `createGeometryMask()` with `createMask()`
- `core/example-games/gym/scenes/GymOverlayUiScene.ts` — Replace `GeometryMask` with `Mask` filter
- `core/src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts` — Verify SVG textures survive WebGL
- `core/src/core-engine/TestGamePool.ts` — Confirm tests still use Canvas (no change needed)
- `core/src/ui/createCardGame.ts` — Already defaults to `Phaser.AUTO`; no change needed

## Existing state

- `createCardGame` already defaults to `Phaser.AUTO` — the Canvas restriction is applied via explicit `type: Phaser.CANVAS` overrides in `main.ts` and `game-repo-scaffold.ts`.
- `TestGamePool` and all browser tests explicitly pass `type: Phaser.CANVAS` for CI performance. This pattern should be preserved.
- GeometryMask is used in ~10+ files across Main Street, core UI, and gym scenes.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk: Mask API compatibility.** The Phaser 4 `Mask` filter API may differ from `GeometryMask` in how it handles dynamic shapes (scrollable content areas, street map clipping). Mitigation: verify each usage with visual testing.
- **Risk: WebGL context loss.** If the GPU driver resets, the game may need to re-initialise textures. Mitigation: implement a basic context-loss listener that logs the event; full restoration can be deferred.
- **Risk: Visual regression.** Thumbnail/visual-regression tests may produce different output under WebGL vs Canvas. Mitigation: update baseline images if acceptable.
- **Assumption: Main Street does not use exotic WebGL blend modes.** Verified — no exotic blend modes in use.
- **Assumption: SVG `addCanvas` textures work under WebGL.** Unverified — requires testing.

## Scope creep

- This work item does **not** implement the GPU card shader — it only enables the WebGL renderer. The card shader itself is tracked in `MS-0MUWNTQ5L0075Y38` (Canvas-compatible effect delivered) and a follow-up item for the GPU version.
- WebGPU is explicitly out of scope — Phaser 4.0.0-rc.7 does not include it.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should the renderer be `Phaser.AUTO` (WebGL with automatic Canvas fallback) or `Phaser.WEBGL` (WebGL only, no fallback)?
  — Answer (work item description): `Phaser.AUTO` — "WebGL with Canvas fallback" stated explicitly.
- Q: Should the priority be elevated from `low` to `high` since this is a prerequisite for GPU shaders?
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): Keep `low` for now. The parent card shader item delivered a Canvas-compatible effect (Option A), so the WebGL migration is not blocking current delivery. Priority remains `low`.
- Q: What specific WebGL-only feature should the browser test exercise?
  — Answer: The test should force `Phaser.WEBGL` and verify that at least one rendering path that relies on WebGL-specific behaviour (e.g., texture filtering, mask rendering, or a simple filter) produces correct output.

# Remote hosting of card packs (remote bundle source) — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

Card packs are currently discovered from a single source: a content directory
(the Electron launcher) or, since `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` landed, a bundled
build-time registry (the browser). There is no mechanism for hosting a pack
catalogue remotely, so publishing or updating a pack forces a rebuild and
re-release of the game. This item implements the **remote source provider** on
top of the pack-source registry abstraction (`PackSource[]` /
`PackSourceRegistry`) introduced by `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`.

## Users

- **Distribution operator** — hosts a signed pack catalogue at a URL and
  expects packs to appear in players' Card Packs panels without rebuilding the
  game.
- **Main Street player** — experiences remote packs identically to bundled
  packs (lock → purchase → enable → deal) and continues to play offline on
  bundled packs when the remote host is unreachable.

Example user stories:

> As a distribution operator, I want to host a card pack catalogue at a URL
> that the game verifies with a signed manifest, so I can publish or update
> packs for an installed game without rebuilding the launcher or the web build.

> As a player, I want remote packs to appear in my Card Packs panel and behave
> exactly like bundled packs, while the game still boots and plays offline on
> bundled packs if the remote host is unreachable.

## Locked design decisions (producer, 2026-10-17)

- **Q1 — Configuration: build-time config constant.** Remote source URLs are
  declared in a build-time config constant (e.g. an environment variable read
  by `vite.config.ts` / a config module), matching the bundled-source pattern.
  No runtime URL mutation in this iteration; launcher-supplied or well-known
  URLs are a possible follow-up.
- **Q2 — Integrity: signed manifests (Ed25519).** Remote manifests are signed
  (Ed25519); the game verifies the signature against a pinned public key before
  trusting any remote pack content. A manifest that fails verification is
  rejected whole (no packs from that source) with a logged warning — safe
  refusal, never a crash. Host allow-list remains as the first gate (only
  configured URLs are fetched at all).
- **Q3 — Timeout & degradation: bounded hard timeout, console-only warning.**
  A hard fetch timeout (≈3 s) bounds the boot path; on failure the game boots
  on bundled packs and logs a warning to the console. **No UI change** — no
  toast, no panel indicator. The Card Packs listing is never empty when a
  bundled pack exists.
- **Q4 — Merge precedence: bundled always wins.** When the same pack id
  appears in more than one source, the **bundled source wins**; a remote pack
  can never override bundled core content. This is implemented by keeping the
  bundled source registered *before* the remote source in the registry (the
  registry's first-wins consultation order) plus an explicit test asserting the
  precedence.

## Scope

1. **Remote source provider.** Implement a `PackSource` (`createRemotePackSource`)
   that fetches a pack manifest and pack CSVs from a configured base URL via
   the loader's existing `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` transport seam and
   contributes its packs to the merged pool.
2. **Configuration.** Declare remote source URLs as a build-time config
   constant (e.g. `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` or a config module), consumed when the
   default registry is built. Multiple remote sources compose additively in
   registration order, always **after** the bundled source.
3. **Merge and precedence.** Pack-id precedence is deterministic: bundled wins
   over remote (remote registered after bundled). Pack-id conflicts between two
   remote sources resolve first-wins (registration order). The core merge
   contract continues to reject duplicate card ids whole.
4. **Gating.** Remote packs remain content-unlock gated; the unlock target key
   and the scoped simulated-purchase flow apply unchanged. Remote packs are not
   automatically ungated.
5. **Degradation.** A remote host that is slow, unreachable, or serving a
   malformed manifest degrades to the bundled/static packs with a warning —
   never blocks boot, never blanks the listing. A bounded timeout (≈3 s) is
   applied to the manifest fetch (and per-file fetches).
6. **Trust and integrity.** Remote manifests are **Ed25519-signed**; the game
   verifies the signature against a pinned public key before trusting content.
   Failure modes: bad signature / missing signature / malformed manifest →
   reject source whole with a warning. Host allow-list: only configured URLs
   are fetched.
7. **Caching / offline.** No client-side caching of remote packs in this
   iteration — remote packs require the remote host at load time; the offline
   story is the bundled packs. Cache in `localStorage` / Cache Storage is a
   recorded follow-up.
8. **Docs and tests.** Cover remote discovery, signed-manifest verification,
   degradation, gating, precedence and asset resolution with tests; document
   the remote-hosting contract (configuration, signing, hosting layout,
   degradation).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Remote discovery.** A pack catalogue hosted at a configured (build-time)
   URL is fetched at runtime and its packs appear in the Card Packs panel
   alongside bundled packs.
2. **Parity.** Remote packs behave identically to bundled packs across the full
   lock → purchase → enable → deal flow, including save/load persistence.
3. **Degradation.** When the remote host is unreachable, slow, or serves a
   malformed manifest, the game boots on bundled packs and logs a warning; the
   Card Packs listing is never empty when a bundled pack exists; the fetch is
   bounded by a timeout (≈3 s) so boot is never blocked.
4. **Rejection of bad data.** A malformed remote manifest or a pack with a bad
   header/duplicate id is rejected whole with a logged warning, without
   affecting packs from other sources.
5. **Deterministic precedence.** Bundled packs always win over remote packs
   with the same pack id; conflicts between remote sources resolve
   first-wins in registration order; precedence is explicit and tested.
6. **Signed-manifest integrity.** A remote manifest whose Ed25519 signature is
   missing, invalid, or not produced by the pinned key is rejected whole with a
   logged warning and no packs from that source are loaded; the failure mode is
   documented.
7. **Asset resolution.** Remote pack art resolves and renders correctly,
   coordinated with `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` (pack assets self-contained) — remote
   assets resolve through the environment-injected `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls`
   seam.
8. **Documentation.** README / packs README / DEPLOYMENT documentation covers
   remote configuration, the hosting contract (layout, signing), integrity and
   degradation.
9. **Testing.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes; remote
   discovery, signature verification, degradation, precedence, gating and asset
   resolution are covered by automated tests.

## Constraints

- **Reuse existing seams.** The remote source consumes the existing injectable
  `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` / `fetchAsset` transports on the loader
  (`createPackSourceTransports`); no core loader changes.
- **Totality.** The remote source never throws: network failures, timeouts,
  malformed responses, signature failures, and missing files all resolve to
  `null` and the core loader degrades to bundled/static packs.
- **Additive.** The remote source is added to the existing
  `PackSourceRegistry` **after** the bundled source, without modifying bundled
  or content-directory sources.
- **Bounded timeout.** Remote fetches on the boot path are bounded (≈3 s) so
  the game never stalls waiting for a slow or hung host.
- **Signing key separation.** The pinned verification public key is a build-time
  constant; the private signing key is held by the distribution operator and is
  never shipped in the game.
- **Pack content stays licence-clean.** Remote packs must satisfy the same
  licence requirements as bundled packs (documented in the hosting contract).
- **No runtime URL mutation** in this iteration (build-time config only).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` — `createRemotePackSource`, signature
  verification, registration and precedence.
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — remote source configuration + transport
  wiring (consumes the `packSources` option).
- `vite.config.ts` / config module (e.g. `src/mainStreetRemotePacks.ts`) —
  build-time remote URL + pinned public key declaration.
- `src/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — remote source boot wiring.
- `core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts` — transport usage (should not need changes).
- `tests/main-street/` — remote discovery, signature verification, degradation,
  precedence, asset-resolution tests.
- `README.md`, `packs/README.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md` — remote-hosting contract.

## Out of scope

- A pack storefront, purchase/checkout, or pack-authoring UI.
- A pack CDN/build-publish pipeline or signing tooling UI (a natural follow-up
  — the signing key/algorithm contract is defined here, tooling later).
- Real money/Steam storefront transactions.
- Changing the bundled or content-directory sources.
- Client-side caching of remote packs for offline use (recorded follow-up).
- Runtime/launcher-supplied remote URL mutation (build-time config only).

## Related work

- **`MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`** — Make card packs available in the browser
  distribution: provides `PackSource` / `PackSourceRegistry`; **blocks** this
  item (this item depends on it). Completed and shipped.
- **`MS-0MV26K321003MWO0`** — Make card-pack assets self-contained: pack art
  resolves from pack assets; remote assets must consume the
  `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls` seam. Completed and shipped.
- **`MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY`** — Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import:
  parent context for the DLC channel.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — supply chain.** Remote content is untrusted; a hostile pack could
  inject arbitrary card data. *Mitigation:* Ed25519-signed manifests verified
  against a pinned public key; host allow-list; safe refusal (reject whole,
  log warning, never crash).
- **Risk — signing overhead.** Key management, signing tooling, and
  verification bugs. *Mitigation:* verification is a small, isolated,
  well-tested function; private key never ships; the public key is pinned at
  build time; signing tooling can be a follow-up (the contract is defined).
- **Risk — boot latency.** A remote fetch on the boot path could stall the
  game. *Mitigation:* bounded timeout (≈3 s), non-blocking degradation,
  bundled-first registry order.
- **Risk — offline regression.** A user who once fetched a remote pack cannot
  use it offline. *Mitigation:* explicit decision — no remote caching this
  iteration; bundled packs remain the offline story; caching recorded as a
  follow-up.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Caching, signing tooling, runtime URL mutation, and a
  pack CDN are natural follow-ups. *Mitigation:* recorded as out of scope /
  linked follow-ups, not built here.
- **Assumption — registry seam exists.** `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` provides the
  `PackSource` abstraction; this item adds a provider rather than
  re-architecting.
- **Assumption — transport seams are adequate.** The existing
  `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` / `fetchAsset` transports can serve a remote
  source without core changes.
- **Assumption — Ed25519 available.** A small Ed25519 verification
  implementation (e.g. WebCrypto `crypto.subtle`/`Ed25519`, or a tiny
  dependency) is available in the browser and test environments; the exact
  mechanism is an implementation detail the implementer records.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Configuration mechanism** (how remote source URLs are declared:
  build-time constant / launcher setting / well-known URL). — **Answer
  (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-17): A — build-time config constant.**
  Matches the bundled-source pattern; simplest; runtime URL mutation is a
  recorded follow-up. Source: worklog comment `MS-C0MVC8TJJA0030X19`.
- **Q2 — Pack-integrity model** (host allow-list / allow-list + checksum /
  signed manifests). — **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-17):
  C — signed manifests (Ed25519).** Verification against a pinned public key;
  failure rejects the source whole with a warning. Source: worklog comment

# Intake Brief — End of game stats (MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV)

## Problem statement

The Main Street **Game Over** overlay currently presents only a *static*
end-of-run snapshot (per-player rows, score breakdown, challenges). Players
cannot see **how their economy evolved turn by turn**, so they cannot tell what
worked and what did not, or learn from a failed run. This item adds per-turn
history tracking to the game state and a **third column of end-of-game
graphs** (profit per turn, cash, businesses, staff and reputation at end of
turn), with the **cash-at-end-of-turn** figure surfaced on the Summary column
and a link to the detailed stats.

## Users

- **Main Street player at game over** — wants a visual run recap instead of
  just a final number.
  - *As a player, I want to see my cash, reputation, businesses and staff
    change turn by turn, so I can understand what worked and improve my next
    run.*
- **Competitive player** — wants the same trajectory for their own seat, so a
  loss against AI can be diagnosed.
- **Balance team / designers** — benefit from a deterministic, serialisable
  per-turn series they can inspect (and reuse for analytics).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Per-turn history captured.** A new `turnStatsHistory` series records one
   snapshot per completed turn — `{ turn, coins, reputation, score, profit,
   businesses, staff }` — where `profit` is the turn's net coin delta
   (reusing the existing `weekStartCoins` snapshot). The snapshot is recorded
   on **both** the deferred (`deferResourceApplication`) and legacy end-of-turn
   paths, and is never recorded twice for the same turn.
2. **Persistence.** `turnStatsHistory` is serialised in
   `MainStreetSerializedState` and restored by `deserializeMainStreetState`;
   legacy saves without the field load with an empty history (no crash, no
   fabricated data).
3. **Graphs.** The Game Over overlay renders a **third column** containing
   composed graphs for: **profit per turn**, **cash at end of turn**,
   **businesses at end of turn**, **staff at end of turn**, and **reputation
   at end of turn**.
4. **Summary cash line + link.** The Summary column shows the final
   **Cash at end of turn** figure, and provides a link/affordance to the
   detailed stats column.
5. **Both modes and layout.** The overlay works in single-player and
   competitive mode and fits the 1280×720 viewport without text clipping or
   vertical overflow; the existing Game State and Summary content is retained.
6. **Overlay conventions.** The new UI honours the established conventions:
   Phaser-free pure model for series data, `hudContainer` parenting, depths
   199 (backdrop) / 200 (box) / 201 (interactive), everything pushed into
   `overlayObjects`; the overlay reads committed state only (no mutation),
   adds no animation (reduced-motion safe) and returns early in
   `scene.replayMode`.
7. **Testing.** Unit tests cover per-turn capture (both paths, no
   double-record), serialise/deserialise round-trip and legacy fallback, and
   the pure series model; browser tests assert the third column and the cash
   line render in both modes.
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Producer decisions (see Appendix):**
  - Target project is **`tce-main-street`** (the item was mis-filed in the
    ContextHub worklog; relocated as this item).
  - **Per-turn history = Option A.** The save game does **not** hold a full
    per-turn history — only the current-turn `weekStartCoins/Rep/Score`
    snapshot — so a new per-turn series must be added, **reusing the existing
    snapshot mechanism/pattern** (persisted alongside the save, legacy
    fallback).
  - **Charting = external charting library** (producer Q3 = B; e.g. Chart.js),
    not hand-rolled Phaser Graphics (A) or SVG-as-texture (C).
  - **No additional stats** beyond the five listed (producer Q4 = "No").
  - **Layout = add a third column** to the Game Over overlay (producer Q5),
    rather than a separate full-page stats screen.
- Game engine is **Phaser `4.0.0-rc.7`**; overlay rendering lives in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`.
- External chart library integration with the Phaser canvas must not regress
  headless/Monte-Carlo runs or replay mode (chart module is skipped there).
- CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** (managed by the ship pipeline); no CI/CD
  pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- **Game Over overlay:** `showGameOverOverlay()` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — two columns (**Game State** /
  **Summary**) with a top band (title + end-reason headline) and the
  Play Again / Menu controls anchored at the panel bottom (panel is 900 px
  wide, laid out by `panelW` / `colW` / `colGap`). The pure, Phaser-free
  content model is `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`
  (`buildGameOverPlayerRows`, `buildGameOverChallengeSummary`,
  `formatEndReason`).
- **Current-turn snapshot:** `state.weekStartCoins` / `weekStartRep` /
  `weekStartScore` are set in `executeWeekStart`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`) and serialised in
  `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`. The per-turn net row
  (`appendTurnNetRow`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`) derives the
  turn's deltas from that snapshot and logs
  `Turn <n> net: <deltas> (score: <delta>)`.
- **Ledger history:** `EconomyLedger.getHistory()`
  (`core/src/rule-engine/EconomyLedger.ts`, imported as
  `@rule-engine/EconomyLedger`) records *every mutation*, is **not
  serialised**, and is **not per-turn** — unsuitable as-is for the graphs.
- **Counts available at turn end:** businesses = non-null entries in
  `state.streetGrid`; staff = `state.staffCards.length`; cash/reputation =
  `state.resourceBank`; score = `state.finalScore`.
- **Precedent:** the Monte Carlo harness already captures a per-turn series
  (`economyHistory: [{ turn, coins, reputation, score }]`) in
  `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` for balance analytics — a useful shape to
  mirror.
- **Save/load:** `serializeMainStreetState` / `deserializeMainStreetState`
  in `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`, with legacy fallbacks for absent
  fields.

## Desired change

1. **State.** Add a `TurnStatSnapshot` interface (`turn`, `coins`,
   `reputation`, `score`, `profit`, `businesses`, `staff`) and
   `turnStatsHistory: TurnStatSnapshot[]` to `MainStreetState`; initialise it
   to `[]` in `setupMainStreetGame` / `createCompetitiveState`.
2. **Capture.** Record one snapshot at the end of each completed turn —
   covering the **deferred** path (`finishDeferredTurnClosing`, after deltas
   are applied) and the **legacy** path — so the turn's net profit is computed
   against `weekStartCoins` exactly like `appendTurnNetRow`. Guard against
   double-recording when the two paths overlap (e.g. keyed by `turn`).
3. **Persistence.** Serialise `turnStatsHistory`; on load, default to `[]`
   for legacy saves.
4. **Model.** Extend `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` with a pure
   series builder (e.g. `buildGameOverStatSeries(state)`) returning the five
   requested series plus the final "cash at end of turn" value.
5. **Render.** Add a **third column** to `showGameOverOverlay()` rendering the
   graphs via the chosen external charting library (encapsulated in a small
   helper module so the model stays Phaser-free and testable), and add the
   **Cash at end of turn** line plus a link to the stats column on the Summary
   column. Recompute `panelW` / column widths / `panelH` so all three columns
   fit the 1280×720 viewport.
6. **Guardrails.** Skip chart construction in `scene.replayMode` / headless
   mode; keep the pure model testable without booting Phaser or the chart
   library.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Add `TurnStatSnapshot` + `turnStatsHistory`
  to `MainStreetState`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — Initialise `turnStatsHistory: []` for
  single-player and competitive setups.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — Record the per-turn snapshot on both
  closing paths (reuse the `weekStartCoins`/`appendTurnNetRow` pattern).
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — Serialise/restore `turnStatsHistory`
  with a legacy `[]` fallback.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — New pure series builder
  (`buildGameOverStatSeries`) + final cash-at-end-of-turn value.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Third column rendering + Summary
  cash line + link; widen/rebalance the panel layout.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — **New** thin wrapper around the
  external charting library (skipped in replay/headless).
- `package.json` — Add the charting-library dependency.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-stats.test.ts` — **New** unit tests (capture,
  round-trip, legacy fallback, series model).
- `tests/main-street/game-over-overlay.test.ts` /
  `tests/main-street/game-over.browser.test.ts` — Third-column and cash-line
  assertions.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` / `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` —
  Document per-turn history and the end-of-game stats column.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM** – Provide reason for game ending (completed) — the
  epic that built the current Game Over overlay.
- **MS-0MUWE6NCA008LDXM** – Two-column Game Over overlay (completed) — the
  layout this item extends to a third column.
- **MS-0MUWE6MA30038RGY** – Game-over summary test harness (completed) — the
  fixture/helper pattern to reuse for tests.
- **MS-0MUWNTJIK009O6BZ** – Credit AI challenge completions to the AI seat
  (completed) — introduced the per-seat Game Over breakdown.
- **MS-0MUNB4ZXQ0081EX7** – Storyline coverage analytics in Monte Carlo
  harness (open) — consumes a per-turn economy series, the same shape this
  item persists.
- **Related docs:** `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§ Activity Log —
  Effective Deltas and Per-Turn Net, § Win conditions),
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`.
- Automated find-related report appended below (if produced).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — external chart library vs Phaser canvas.** Chart.js needs a canvas
  context; overlaying it on the Phaser canvas and keeping it out of
  headless/replay runs needs care. *Mitigation:* isolate the library behind
  `MainStreetStatsChart.ts`, lazy-load/skip in replay/headless, verify bundle
  size.
- **Risk — deferred vs legacy capture paths** could double-record or miss the
  final turn. *Mitigation:* record keyed by `turn` in the shared closing tail,
  with targeted unit tests for both paths.
- **Risk — save/load compatibility.** *Mitigation:* legacy fallback to `[]`,
  with a round-trip + legacy test.
- **Risk — three-column overflow at 1280×720.** *Mitigation:* recompute panel
  width/height and add a browser fit assertion.
- **Assumption — competitive-mode series scope.** In single-player the five
  series describe the run's economy. In competitive mode the shared
  `resourceBank` is seat-scoped during a turn; this brief assumes the graphs
  show the **human seat's** trajectory. *Open question, recorded in the
  Appendix* — the producer may instead want every seat as a separate series.
- **Assumption — "link to a more detailed screen" is satisfied by the third
  column**, per producer Q5; no separate scene is added.
- **Scope-creep risk:** additional stats or chart types beyond the five listed
  (producer Q4 = none) must be raised as separate work items, not folded in.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Correct project?** This item was created in ContextHub (the Worklog
  CLI tool) but describes a Main Street game screen.
  - **Answer (producer): `tce-main-street`.** Source: interactive reply,
    2026-10-16. *Action:* item relocated — created as MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV in
    `tce-main-street`; the mis-filed WL-0MTCMVIPS007AB02 was closed as a
    relocated duplicate.

- **Q2 — Per-turn history tracking.** The save holds only the current-turn
  `weekStartCoins/Rep/Score` snapshot; a full per-turn history must be added
  unless the save already carries one.
  - (A) Add per-turn history tracking, reusing the snapshot mechanism.
    **Recommended.**
  - (B) Use only static current values (no historical graphs).
  - **Answer (producer):** "Doesn't the save game have that snapshot? If not A
    otherwise reuse that mechanism." *Research:* inspected
    `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — the save persists only the **current**
    `weekStart*` snapshot, not a per-turn series; the `EconomyLedger` history
    is per-mutation and not serialised. Therefore **Option A** applies, reusing
    the `weekStart*` snapshot pattern and persisting a new series. Source:
    interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q3 — Chart/graph approach.**
  - (A) Phaser-based line/bar charts (custom `Graphics`). **Recommended** at
    the time of asking (no new dependency).
  - (B) External charting library (e.g. Chart.js).
  - (C) SVG line plots rendered as Phaser textures.
  - **Answer (producer): B** — use an external charting library (overrode the
    recommendation). Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q4 — Additional stats?** Beyond profit/turn, businesses, cash, staff and
  reputation at end of turn.
  - **Answer (producer): No.** Only the five listed stats. Source:
    interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q5 — Summary-screen placement / detailed screen.** "Place the cash at end
  of turn on the summary screen and add a link to a more detailed screen" — is
  the Summary column the right place, with a button to a full-page graph view?
  - **Answer (producer): Add a third column.** The detailed graphs live in a
    third column of the Game Over overlay rather than a separate screen.
    Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **OPEN QUESTION (competitive-mode series scope).** In competitive mode,
  should the graphs plot (i) only the human seat's trajectory, or (ii) every
  seat as a separate series? *Working assumption: (i) human seat only.* Noted
  for producer confirmation during review; not blocking.

# Intake brief: Port the Vite watcher-ignore (`server.watch.ignored`) guard to sibling game repos' `vite.config.ts`

## Problem statement

The core scaffold template (CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA) emits `server.watch.ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS]` (covering `**/.worklog/**` and the dev-output trees), and `tce-main-street` and `tce-the-rising` already carry the block — but 8 sibling game repos' checked-in `vite.config.ts` still lack it: `AI_Hell`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-coloretto`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-golf`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-sushi-go`. When any of these repos accumulates `.worklog/worktrees/**` checkouts (AI_Hell already has 9 + a nested `ToneForge` checkout), the Vite/Vitest file watcher recursively walks them and exhausts the host `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` budget — `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached` — crashing the dev server and breaking test runs (the exact failure mode fixed in the parent item MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY).

## Users

- **Developers/agents working in any Tableau-Card-Engine game repo** (tce-\*) — must be able to run `npm run dev` and `npm test` from the main checkout once worktrees exist without tripping the host watcher limit.
  - *User story:* "As a developer in tce-blackjack, I want my dev server to ignore `.worklog/worktrees/**` so a recursive watch never exhausts inotify (ENOSPC)."
- **AI_Hell maintainers** (in scope — Q1 answered) — same failure mode is already active (9 worktree checkouts).
  - *User story:* "As an AI_Hell developer, I want the same watcher guard, so my `vite` dev server survives `.worklog/worktrees/**` growth."
- **Verification/audit tooling** — full-suite runs in sibling repos must not fail with ENOSPC.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Watcher guard present in every in-scope repo's checked-in config.** The 7 tce-\* repos each import `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` from `./core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin` and set `server.watch.ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS]` with the template's explanatory comment (wording as in CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA / `tce-the-rising`). AI_Hell (if in scope) sets `watch.ignored` from a locally defined constant covering `**/.worklog/**` (plus its dev-output trees). Verified per repo by grep of the checked-in file — no in-scope repo may lack the block.
2. **Per-repo regression guard test (mirrors the core/main-street ENOSPC guard).** Each tce-\* repo gains `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (copy of main-street's, minus the in-process dev-server smoke; static assertions only): the real config imports the shared list, spreads it into `server.watch.ignored`, and the list covers `**/.worklog/**` plus `**/data/**`, `**/tmp/**`, `**/results/**`, `**/dist/**`. AI_Hell gains `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` asserting its local list covers `.worklog`. Each test is picked up by that repo's existing test projects and passes.
3. **Surgical port only.** No other template drift is synced: no `resolvePagesBase`/`base` backfill, no blind re-scaffold (sibling configs predate those template additions), no local-config changes (e.g. AI_Hell's `configCsvPlugin`, `open: true`, port settings) altered. Per-repo `git diff` touches only `vite.config.ts` plus the new guard test; pre-existing unrelated working-tree changes (`.gitignore`, untracked `AGENTS.md`/`.githooks/`/`.worklog/plugins/`) are never swept into a commit.
4. **Suites pass and changes land on each repo's `dev`.** Each in-scope repo's own test suite passes (agent-initiated runs go through the test skill, per repo), and each repo's change is committed on its `dev` branch and pushed to origin, with commits referencing `MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0` (precedent: cross-repo item MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV). The pre-existing 1-ahead-unpushed local commit on each sibling `dev` is accounted for at push time (see Constraints). tce-main-street itself has no source changes, so its suite is unaffected; full project suite (each modified repo) must pass with the changes.
5. **Documentation reflects the guard.** Config comment matches the core template wording; where a repo documents `npm run dev` (README/dev docs — currently none of the in-scope repos has a README), a matching note about the `.worklog/**` exclusion. CHANGELOG.md excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **No core/TCE repository edits and no submodule moves.** The core scaffold template and its guard tests are already correct (CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA completed) and every sibling's pinned core commit (`09723c4b`) already exports `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` in `scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` — verified.
- **Surgical only** — do **not** blind re-scaffold (`npm run scaffold` / `scaffold:games`): the current template additionally emits `resolvePagesBase`/production `base` behaviour that the sibling configs do not have; a re-scaffold would change more than the watch block. Port the `server.watch.ignored` block + import only.
- **Cross-repo working-tree isolation.** This item lives in tce-main-street's worklog but touches 8 sibling checkouts, all outside the tce-main-street worktree. Precedent MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV ("Cross-repo change ... Pushed to sibling dev") governs: edit each sibling checkout directly, commit per repo on its own `dev`, push per repo. tce-main-street's own worktree/main checkout stays untouched (no tce-main-street source change → no implement-worktree changes expected).
- **Respect pre-existing dirt.** Each sibling has unrelated uncommitted changes (`.gitignore` edits; untracked `AGENTS.md`, `.githooks/`, `.worklog/plugins/`). Never commit them; stage only `vite.config.ts` (+ new test).
- **Sibling `dev` is 1 commit ahead of origin** (an unpushed `.worklog/config.yaml` CTA commit, `WL-0MUWCGF670087GAS`). Pushing the port will carry that commit; if a non-fast-forward/push rejection occurs, resolve against that known baseline (do not rewrite others' pushed history).
- **Test-execution policy:** all agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill — run per repo (each sibling has its own CWD/worklog), never ad-hoc `npm test`/`vitest`.

## Existing state

- **Scaffolded siblings (7):** `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-coloretto`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-golf`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-sushi-go` — `vite.config.ts` is AUTO-GENERATED (scaffold `renderViteConfig`), identical to each other apart from the game name in the header comment, and each `server:` block has `port: 3000, open: false` only — no `watch.ignored`. Verified: `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` absent from all 7.
- **AI_Hell (1):** bespoke hand-written config (port 5173, `open: true`, `configCsvPlugin`, no `core` submodule) — no `server.watch` at all; it **cannot** import the core list. It already has 9 `.worklog/worktrees/**` checkouts (+ nested `ToneForge` checkout) — the ENOSPC failure mode is live there.
- **Exemplars:** `tce-main-street/vite.config.ts` and `tce-the-rising/vite.config.ts` already carry the block (main-street also has `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts`, the regression pattern to mirror; core has `game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` static guard).
- Siblings' core submodules are clean and pinned at `v0.1.17-201-g09723c4b`, which exports `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS`. Their `npm test` = `vitest run --project unit` with `include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']`, and tsconfig includes `tests/**/*.ts` — new config tests are picked up automatically.

## Desired change

- **Per tce-\* repo:** in `vite.config.ts`, add `import { DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS } from './core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin';` and extend the `server:` block with `watch: { ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS] }` + the template's ENOSPC comment; add `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (static assertions copied from main-street's guard).
- **AI_Hell (in scope — Q1 answered):** add a locally defined ignore constant (e.g. `vite/watchIgnore.ts`) mirroring the core list (or a scoped `.worklog`-focused list), wire `server: { watch: { ignored: [...] } }` into `vite.config.ts`, and add `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts`.
- Single source of truth stays in core; nothing in `core/` changes.

## Key Files:

- Each tce-\* repo: `vite.config.ts` — add `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` import + `server.watch.ignored` block
- Each tce-\* repo: `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (new) — static config-wiring + pattern-coverage guard (mirror of `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` ENOSPC assertions and main-street's `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts`)

## Related work

- MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY — Host inotify watcher exhaustion (ENOSPC) breaks main-checkout test runs (**parent; completed**; this item is its derived sibling port)
- CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA — core: `game-repo-scaffold` renderViteConfig omits `server.watch.ignored` (completed; template now emits it)
- CG-0MTJ7A4Z3000MFMV / CG-0MTJ560IZ005XAZC — core: vite-transcript-plugin ENOSPC hardening (completed)
